# Emissions and emissions trading {#sec-emissions}

This chapter turns the fuel use of @sec-demand, @sec-power and @sec-transport into emissions. It covers carbon
dioxide from fuel combustion, the other greenhouse gases of the national inventory, methane by source with the
methane fee, the comparison with the country's NDC, and the local air pollutants. It closes with the new emissions
trading system (ETS): how its cap becomes a permit price, and how that price enters fuel prices and revenue.

Emissions matter twice in the model. They are an output (the GHG path of each scenario, the change against the
baseline, the gap to the NDC) and they feed back: CO2 emission factors convert every carbon price into a price per
unit of fuel (@sec-prices), and covered emissions set the ETS price. The carbon pricing indicators (coverage of the
carbon tax and the ETS, effective carbon rates, revenue per tonne) are described with the revenues in @sec-fiscal.

The methodology describes emissions in
[methodology, section 3.5](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#emissions), the local pollutants in
[methodology, section 6.4](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/06_Air_pollution.html#sec-calc_em) and the ETS price in
[methodology, section 3.2.4](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#sec-PricesForecastedYears) and
[Appendix C](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#sec-Appendix_C_Prices).

## Overview {#sec-em-overview}

### Order of calculation {#sec-em-order}

The ETS price is set before the year loop, with the other policies: it depends only on inputs and on stored
baseline emissions, never on the fuel use of the year. Inside each year, the emission blocks run after fuel use and
power, in this order.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  P["Policies (all years):<br/>ETS cap and price,<br/>methane fee"] --> F["Year t: power,<br/>fuel use"]
  F --> C["CO2 by sector, fuel,<br/>ETS sector; ETS check"]
  C --> G["Methane by source,<br/>GHG inventory categories"]
  G --> A["Local air<br/>pollutants"]
  A --> K["Kaya identity"]
  K --> N["After the last year:<br/>NDC comparison"]
```

The CO2 of each subsector and fuel is computed inside the fuel-use block (@sec-demand), and the CO2 of each
generation type inside the power block (@sec-power); this chapter gives the equation once and builds the totals.
The NDC rows run after the year loop because they read the baseline in the NDC target year.

### Notation and units {#sec-em-notation}

Every equation holds for each scenario $o$ and country $c$; these indices are omitted. A value of the baseline
(scenario 1) in the same year carries the superscript $B$; the previous year carries $t-1$. Other indices:

| Index | Set |
|---|---|
| $s$ | subsector (16; @sec-demand), or a coverage sector $e$ (power and the 16 subsectors, 17 in all) |
| $f$ | fuel (8, plus jet fuel for CO2), or generation type $k$ (9; @sec-power) |
| $u$ | UNFCCC inventory category: energy, industrial processes (IPPU), agriculture, LULUCF, waste, other |
| $p$ | gas: CO2, CH4, N2O, F-gases; or local pollutant: PM2.5, NOx, SO2, VOC, BC, OC, CO |
| $j$ | methane source: oil and gas, downstream gas, coal mining, biomass, livestock, rice, waste |
| $t$ | year, from the base year $t_0$ to 2041; $Y$ is the last year of the country's GHG inventory |

Units: CO2 in Mt; other greenhouse gases in Mt CO2e with the IPCC AR6 GWP100 (fossil methane 29.8, non-fossil
methane 27.2); methane by source in kt CH4; local pollutants in kt; fuel use in ktoe. $\theta$ is PJ per ktoe
(0.041868), so fuel use (ktoe) $\times\ \theta\ \times$ a factor in t CO2 per GJ gives Mt CO2. For Egypt $Y$ = 2024.

## Energy CO2 {#sec-em-co2}

Energy CO2 is fuel use times an emission factor, for every subsector, fuel and generation type. The factors are
those of the country, scaled once so that the model's base year matches the national inventory. The methodology
describes this in
[methodology, sections 3.5.3 and 3.5.4.1](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#carbon-dioxide-co_2).

### Emission factors {#sec-em-ef}

Each fuel and EF sector has one CO2 factor. The EF sectors are power, road, residential and industry; every
subsector reads one of them:

| EF sector | Subsectors |
|---|---|
| power | power generation (by generation type) |
| road | road, rail, domestic aviation, domestic navigation |
| residential | residential, food & forestry, services |
| industry | the eight industrial subsectors and other energy use |

The factor is looked up in the IIASA (GAINS) table of the country, else of its World Bank region, else of the
world:

$$
ef^{0}_{s,f} = \begin{cases}
ef^{IIASA}_{c \to r \to w}(f', s') / 1000 & \text{fossil fuels} \\
ef^{IEA}_{jet} & f = \text{jet fuel, in every sector} \\
0 & f = \text{biomass}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-em-ef}

where

- $ef^{0}_{s,f}$ is the CO2 factor before calibration, t CO2 per GJ;
- $ef^{IIASA}_{c \to r \to w}$ is the factor of sheet EF_GHG in kg CO2 per GJ, for the country $c$, else its World Bank
  region $r$, else the world $w$ (0 if none), divided by 1000 kg per t;
- $(f', s')$ is the fuel and EF sector the row reads: the row's own, except for the substitutions below;
- $ef^{IEA}_{jet}$ = 0.0715 t CO2 per GJ (IEA, 19.5 tC per TJ $\times$ 44/12), used for jet fuel in every sector
  and in domestic aviation.

Some fuel and sector pairs have no factor of their own. They read another, as the methodology's table of missing
factors:

| Fuel and sector | Factor used |
|---|---|
| coal in road | coal in power |
| LPG in power | LPG in industry |
| LPG in road | LPG in residential |
| kerosene in power and in road | kerosene in residential |
| other oil products in road | diesel in road |
| biomass, every sector | 0 |

The factors of this table are the model's data step ([A7.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A7-1)). The local-pollutant
and combustion-methane factors follow a different chain, described in @sec-em-ap-data.

### Calibration to the GHG inventory {#sec-em-calib}

The IIASA factors include some process and fugitive emissions, and fuel-use data differ between sources. The model
therefore scales every CO2 factor by one number, so that modelled base-year CO2 equals the inventory. This is
legacy CPAT's rule (issue I32, replicated by user decision).

$$
\chi = \frac{CO2^{inv}_{t_0 - 1}}{CO2^{B,raw}_{t_0}}, \qquad ef_{s,f} = \chi\, ef^{0}_{s,f}, \qquad ef_k = \chi\, ef^{0}_k
$$ {#eq-em-calib}

where

- $\chi$ (`EFCalib`) is the calibration factor, 1 when the switch is off;
- $CO2^{inv}_{t_0 - 1}$ is the inventory energy CO2 of the year before the base year (Mt);
- $CO2^{B,raw}_{t_0}$ is scenario-1 energy CO2 of the base year with the uncalibrated factors: the base-year
  energy balance times $ef^{0}$ (Mt);
- $ef_{s,f}$, $ef_k$ are the calibrated factors of subsectors and generation types.

The switch is on by default (`Yes*`), as legacy, whose two switches `EFsAdjustmentAnnexI` and
`EFsAdjustmentNonAnnexI` are both `Yes*`. The model has one switch for all countries.

**Why the baseline value is data.** A live formula for $CO2^{B,raw}$ would be circular: the factors feed the carbon
prices, which feed fuel use. The uncalibrated scenario-1 CO2 is therefore stored as data, keyed by country, and
refreshed by the build, like the ETS baseline (@sec-em-ets-cap). This is exact: scenario-1 fuel use does not depend
on the factors (there is no new carbon price in the baseline, and existing carbon pricing changes only after the
historical years), so the calibrated baseline is the uncalibrated one times $\chi$. Another country finds no stored
rows until the build has been run for it.

**What follows from $\chi$.** Everything downstream uses the calibrated factors: CO2 by subsector, fuel and
generation type; the carbon tax, the ETS cost and existing carbon pricing per unit of fuel and their revenue; the
ETS baseline; energy CO2 in the GHG totals. Scenario-1 fuel use and prices do not change. In policy scenarios,
carbon prices per unit of fuel change by the factor (7% lower for Egypt), so fuel use, revenue and the GDP effect
change too.

### CO2 by subsector, fuel and coverage sector {#sec-em-co2-totals}

With the factors in hand, CO2 is fuel use times the factor ([M7.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M7-1)):

$$
em_{s,f,CO_2} = \theta\, F_{s,f}\, ef_{s,f}, \qquad em_{k,CO_2} = \theta\, PE_k\, ef_k
$$ {#eq-em-co2}

where

- $em_{s,f,CO_2}$ is the CO2 of subsector $s$ and fuel $f$ (Mt), `co2`;
- $F_{s,f}$ is fuel use (ktoe), `ener` (@sec-demand);
- $PE_k$ is the fuel input of generation type $k$ (ktoe), `pe` (@sec-power), and $ef_k$ its factor.

The totals sum over fuels, subsectors and generation types:

$$
em_{CO_2} = \sum_{s}\sum_{f} em_{s,f,CO_2} + \sum_{k} em_{k,CO_2}
$$ {#eq-em-co2tot}

The block also reports CO2 by sector group (transport, buildings, industry, other energy use, power), by fuel
(power fuels included), the baseline value of the same year (`co2.ref`), the change against it (`co2.pct`, `co2.chg`)
and a check that the totals by group and by fuel both equal the total (`co2.chk` = 0). CO2 by coverage sector
(`co2.sec`) feeds the ETS check of @sec-em-ets-cap:

$$
em_{e} = \sum_{f} em_{e,f,CO_2} \ (e \ne \text{power}), \qquad em_{pow} = \sum_k em_{k,CO_2}
$$ {#eq-em-co2sec}

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: energy CO2"}
```
# data step, once per country
for (f, s) in co2_ef_rows:                      # fuel x EF sector (pow, rod, res, ind)
    if f == "jfu":   ef0[f, s] = EFJetIEA        # 0.0715 tCO2/GJ
    elif f == "bio": ef0[f, s] = 0
    else:            ef0[f, s] = pick(country, region, world, source_fuel(f, s), source_sector(f, s)) / 1000
EFCalib = inv_energy_co2[base_year - 1] / stored_raw_co2_s1[base_year] if calibrate else 1
ef = EFCalib * ef0

for t in years:
    for s in subsectors:
        for f in fuels:
            co2[s, f][t] = ener[s, f][t] * PJ_PER_KTOE * ef[f, ef_sector(s)]
    for k in gen_types:
        co2["pow", k][t] = pe[k][t] * PJ_PER_KTOE * ef[k]
    co2_total[t] = sum(co2[s, f][t] for s, f) + sum(co2["pow", k][t] for k)
    co2_sec[e][t] = sum over fuels of co2[e, f][t]    # power: sum over types
    co2_ref[t] = co2_total_baseline[t]
    co2_pct[t] = co2_total[t] / co2_ref[t] - 1
    co2_chk[t] = |co2_total - sum by group| + |co2_total - sum by fuel|    # 0
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** factors on sheet Inputs (CO2 factor rows, `EFSel`), calibration switch Settings C27 (`Yes*`), factor
  Settings C29 (`EFCalib`); stored uncalibrated scenario-1 CO2 on sheet BaselineCO2 (keys `EGY|raw`, `EGY|pow`, ...).
  Rows `co2` in sections 5-8 (subsectors) and 3 (generation types); totals in section 13 (`co2`, `co2.ref`,
  `co2.pct`, `co2.sec`, `co2.chk`, `co2.chg`).
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/ef_data.py`, `co2_efs()` and `co2_calibration()` (EQ-A7.1);
  `fuel_use.py` (CO2 of subsectors, EQ-M7.1), `power.py` (CO2 of generation types); totals in
  `emissions.py`, `co2()`. The calibration reads Excel-AI's stored scenario-1 CO2. See the
  [blocks of CPAT Python](../CPAT_coded_documentation_html/02_How_it_works.html#sec-blocks).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT"}
- **Calibration (issue I32, replicated).** As legacy (Mitigation rows 623, 839, 976-977): the inventory year before
  the base year against the base-year estimate, switch on. Earlier versions of the prototype used the last
  inventory year and had the switch off; the user decided to follow legacy.
- **One switch.** Legacy reads one switch for Annex I countries (ScenarioDefinition row 237) and one for the others,
  both `Yes*`. The model has one switch.
- **Scope.** Inventory energy CO2 includes fugitive CO2 (Egypt: 7.1 Mt in 2024), which the model does not compute
  separately. The factor absorbs it, as in legacy.
- **Inventory break (I91).** Egypt's inventory jumps 19% from 2021 to 2022. Legacy's rule carries this break into
  every year: calibrated CO2 is 16-29% below the 2022-2024 inventory.
- **Methodology.** The methodology scales to the inventory of 2019 and offers global IEA factors as an option. The
  model uses the IIASA factors (IEA only for jet fuel) and the year before the base year.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: results for Egypt"}
With the shipped data, the 2021 inventory is 211.05 Mt against the 2022 estimate of 226.97 Mt:
$\chi$ = 0.930 (legacy: 0.930).

| Year | Inventory | Uncalibrated | Calibrated ($\times$ 0.930) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 252.2 | 227.0 | 211.1 |
| 2023 | 267.4 | 196.7 | 182.9 |
| 2024 | 285.3 | 218.9 | 203.5 |

Energy CO2, scenario 1, Mt. The calibrated base year equals the 2021 inventory (211.1), as legacy. The 2023 dip is
the fuel-use shock of legacy row 483 (issue I92, replicated; @sec-demand).
:::

## Methane by source and the methane fee {#sec-em-methane}

Methane is the second greenhouse gas of most inventories and the one a methane fee targets. The model splits the
inventory's methane between seven sources, projects each with its own activity, lets the fee abate it along the
source's cost curve, and collects the fee revenue. The methodology describes this in
[methodology, section 3.5.4.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#methane-ch_4) (energy methane) and
[sections 3.5.5.2 and 3.5.5.3.1](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#agriculture) (agriculture and
waste).

| Source $j$ | Category | GWP | Activity | Curve |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| oil and gas extraction (`og`) | energy | fossil | oil and gas production | oil and gas |
| downstream gas (`dg`) | energy | fossil | gas use | oil and gas |
| coal mining (`cm`) | energy | fossil | coal production | coal |
| biomass use (`bm`) | energy | fossil | biomass use | oil and gas |
| livestock (`liv`) | agriculture | non-fossil | index of income and population | livestock |
| rice (`ric`) | agriculture | non-fossil | index of income and population | rice |
| waste (`wst`) | waste | non-fossil | index of income and population | waste |

Biomass and downstream gas use the oil-and-gas curve, as legacy. The four energy sources together are the
**fuel-supply methane** (`ch4.sup`).

### Data {#sec-em-ch4-data}

| Sheet | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| GHGs | Inventory by country, year, category (energy, industrial processes, agriculture, LULUCF, waste, other) and gas (CO2, CH4, N2O, F-gases), Mt CO2e | Legacy sheet GHGs |
| CH4Inputs | Methane abatement curves ($A$, $B$) by country and source, with an average (`AVG`) row; shares that split inventory methane by source; flared share | Legacy sheet CH4Inputs |
| EF_NonCO2 | Combustion factors (kt per PJ) by country or region, subsector, fuel and pollutant, base year and final | Legacy sheet EF_PM (GAINS; all countries and World Bank regions) |
| UNPop | Population by country and year (thousands) | Legacy sheet UNPop (UN WPP) |
| Balances | Base-year production of gas, oil and coal | Legacy Mitigation rows 503-509 |
| Prices_int | World production of oil, coal and gas, Mtoe, by IEA scenario | Legacy rows 717-719 |

The other methane inputs are on sheet `Manual inputs`, at the legacy addresses:

| Cell | Input | Default |
|---|---|---|
| J185 | Intensity decline, oil and natural gas (also downstream gas and biomass) | 0.25% per year |
| J186 | Intensity decline, coal | 0 |
| J187 | Intensity decline, agriculture (livestock, rice) | 0.47% per year |
| J188 | Intensity decline, waste | 0.5% per year |
| J190:J192 | Price elasticity of production: oil, coal, natural gas | −0.30, −0.43, −0.46 |
| J194 | Pass-through of the methane fee on fossil fuels to consumers | 0 |
| J196:J200 | Fee applies to: biomass, downstream gas, fossil fuel production (oil, gas, coal), agriculture (livestock, rice), waste | No, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes |

The decline rates are calibrated on US EPA data (legacy notes). The fee switches are named `MFeeBio`, `MFeeDG`,
`MFeeFF`, `MFeeAgr`, `MFeeWst` and shown on sheet Settings. They are legacy inputs outside ScenarioDefinition: the
main inputs are on ScenarioDefinition, `Manual inputs` is the second source.

### The methane fee {#sec-em-mfee}

The fee is a price per tonne of CO2-equivalent methane. It follows a linear path that keeps its slope after the
target year, applies only in policy scenarios, and can add the carbon price
([M1.8](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-8)):

$$
MF_t = \Lambda(t;\, T^{m}_0, T^{m}_1, x^{m}_0, x^{m}_1)\ \mathbb{1}[o \ne B] \;+\; NCT_t\ \mathbb{1}[\texttt{CTforMethane} = \text{Yes}]
$$ {#eq-em-mfee}

where

- $MF_t$ is the methane fee (USD per t CO2e, real), `mfee`;
- $\Lambda$ is the linear policy path of @sec-model-overview, from `MPLevelStart` in `MPIntro` to `MPLevelTarget` in
  `MPOutro`, **continued linearly** after `MPOutro` (as legacy);
- $\mathbb{1}[o \ne B]$ is 1 in policy scenarios (scenario number above 1, legacy row 2238);
- $NCT_t$ is the carbon price (USD per t CO2), added when `CTforMethane` = Yes. This part has no scenario
  condition, as legacy row 2239.

### Allocation of inventory methane to sources {#sec-em-ch4-alloc}

The inventory reports methane by category, not by source. The model splits the methane of the last inventory year
$Y$ between the sources of each category. For the four energy sources, each source's input share is capped by ten
times its share of energy activity, and the capped weights are normalised:

$$
w_j = \min\!\left(\mu\,\frac{X^{0}_j}{\sum_{i \in \text{fossil}} X^{0}_i},\ sh_j\right), \qquad
\pi_j = \frac{w_j}{\sum_{i \in \text{fossil}} w_i} \quad (j \in \text{fossil})
$$ {#eq-em-ch4share}

where

- $sh_j$ is the country's input share of source $j$ (CH4Inputs: oil row `per_upstream_og`, `per_downstream_g`,
  `per_biomass`; coal row `per_upstream_c`), 0 if missing;
- $X^{0}_j$ is the base-year activity of the source (data): oil plus gas production and coal production from
  Balances; gas and biomass use from the energy-consumption data of the first year (every column but electricity);
- $\mu$ = 10 (`MethShareCap`, legacy row 899);
- $\pi_j$ is the share of energy methane allocated to source $j$.

Livestock and rice take their input shares of agricultural methane ($\pi_j = sh_j$, rows `per_livestock`,
`per_rice`); waste takes all waste methane ($\pi_{wst} = 1$). The base emissions of each source, in kt CH4, are then

$$
M_{j,0} = M^{inv}_{u(j),Y}\ \pi_j\ \frac{1000}{GWP_j}
$$ {#eq-em-ch4base}

where

- $M^{inv}_{u(j),Y}$ is the inventory methane of the source's category (energy, agriculture or waste) in year $Y$,
  Mt CO2e (`ghg.invb`);
- $GWP_j$ is 29.8 for the fossil sources and 27.2 for livestock, rice and waste.

The shares and base emissions are data of the country: they are the same in every scenario, so the calibration is
to the observed inventory.

### Activity {#sec-em-ch4-activity}

Each source has an activity that moves its emissions. Downstream gas and biomass follow the scenario's total use of
the fuel (power included), so fuel switching changes their methane. Livestock, rice and waste follow an index
driven by income and population:

$$
X_j(t) = X_j(t-1)\,(1 + g^{pc}_t)^{\epsilon^{Y}_{u(j)}}\,(1 + n_t)^{\epsilon^{N}_{u(j)}}, \qquad X_j(t_0) = 1 \qquad (j \in \{\text{liv}, \text{ric}, \text{wst}\})
$$ {#eq-em-ch4act}

where

- $g^{pc}_t$ is GDP per capita growth and $n_t$ population growth (@eq-em-drivers);
- $\epsilon^{Y}$, $\epsilon^{N}$ are the income and population elasticities of the category: agriculture 0.15 and
  0.9, waste 0 and 1 (@sec-em-other).

The two extraction sources follow fuel production, $X_{og} = Prd_{oil} + Prd_{gas}$ and $X_{cm} = Prd_{coal}$,
described next.

#### Fuel production for supply methane {#sec-em-ch4-prod}

The model has no production model for fossil fuels. Production follows world demand of the global demand scenario,
and responds to the producer price change that the methane fee causes, as legacy rows 6132-6149 (issue I66). First,
the fee per ktoe produced, after abatement:

$$
fk_j(t) = MF_t\, GWP_j\, \iota_j \cdot 1000 \cdot \frac{M_{j,0}}{X^{0}_j}\,(1 - a_j(t)), \qquad fk_j(t_0) = 0 \qquad (j \in \{\text{og}, \text{cm}\})
$$ {#eq-em-ch4fk}

where $\iota_j$ is 1 if the fee applies to the source (fossil fuel production switch), else 0, and $a_j$ the
abatement share of @eq-em-ch4abt. $fk_j$ is in USD per ktoe. Its change raises the producer price index:

$$
\Pi_f(t) = 1 + \frac{fk_{j(f)}(t) - fk_{j(f)}(t-1)}{p^{int}_f(t)\ \gamma_f}\ \phi^{pass}, \qquad \Pi_f(t_0) = 1
$$ {#eq-em-ch4pi}

where

- $j(f)$ is the oil-and-gas source for oil and gas, coal mining for coal;
- $p^{int}_f$ is the international price of the fuel in its own unit (oil per barrel, gas per MMBtu, coal per
  tonne; @sec-prices);
- $\gamma_f$ is price units per ktoe: 41,868 GJ per ktoe divided by 6.1408 GJ per barrel, 1.055056 GJ per MMBtu or
  29.3076 GJ per tonne;
- $\phi^{pass}$ is the pass-through (Manual inputs J194, default 0, so $\Pi_f = 1$ by default).

Production holds the base-year value in the base year and the next, then grows with the price response and with
world demand of the year before:

$$
Prd_f(t) = \begin{cases}
Prd^{0}_f & t \le t_0 + 1 \\
Prd_f(t-1)\ \Pi_f(t)^{\varepsilon_f}\ \dfrac{WD_f(t-1)}{WD_f(t-2)} & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-em-ch4prd}

where

- $Prd^{0}_f$ is base-year production of oil products, coal and gas (Balances, ktoe);
- $\varepsilon_f$ is the price elasticity of production (Manual inputs J190:J192);
- $WD_f$ is world production of the fuel in the IEA scenario `GlobalEnergyDemand` of scenario 1 (Stated Policies,
  Announced Pledges, Sustainable Development, Net Zero), Mtoe. As legacy, the third and fourth options both read the
  Net Zero row.

The source shares use base-year production as their activity, so the shares do not depend on this projection (no
loop).

### Abatement and emissions {#sec-em-ch4-abt}

The fee abates methane along a power-function cost curve of the source ([A7.3](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A7-3)):

$$
a_j(t) = \min\!\Big(1,\ \max\!\big(0,\ A_j\,(MF_t\, GWP_j\, \iota_j)^{B_j}\big)\Big)
$$ {#eq-em-ch4abt}

where

- $a_j$ is the abatement share (`ch4.abt`);
- $MF_t\,GWP_j$ is the fee per tonne of CH4 (USD);
- $A_j$, $B_j$ are the curve coefficients of CH4Inputs (`avg_pow_a`, `avg_pow_b`) for the country and the source's
  curve row; where the country value is 0 or missing, the CH4Inputs average (`AVG`) is used, as legacy
  (issue I152);
- $\iota_j$ is the fee switch of the source (@sec-em-ch4-data).

Methane intensity also declines on its own, from the last inventory year:

$$
I_j(t) = (1 - \delta_j)^{\max(0,\ t - Y)}
$$ {#eq-em-ch4int}

where $I_j$ is the intensity index (`ch4.int`) and $\delta_j$ the source's rate of autonomous technological
improvement (Manual inputs J185:J188; oil and gas also for downstream gas and biomass, issue I141). The emissions of
each source combine base emissions, activity, intensity and abatement:

$$
M_j(t) = M_{j,0}\ \frac{X_j(t)}{X^{0}_j}\ I_j(t)\ \big(1 - a_j(t)\big)
$$ {#eq-em-ch4em}

where $M_j(t)$ is the methane of source $j$ in kt CH4 (`ch4.em`), 0 if $X^{0}_j = 0$. For livestock, rice and waste
$X^{0}_j = 1$. Fuel-supply methane is $M^{sup}(t) = \sum_{j \in \text{fossil}} M_j(t)$.

### Flaring and the fee revenue {#sec-em-ch4-rev}

Part of the abated oil-and-gas methane is flared: it burns to CO2 and is reported as energy CO2.

$$
CO2^{flr}_t = r_{fl}\ \phi_{fl}\ M_{og,0}\ \frac{X_{og}(t)}{X^{0}_{og}}\ a_{og}(t)\ /\ 1000
$$ {#eq-em-flare}

where $CO2^{flr}$ is in Mt (`ghg.flr`), $r_{fl}$ = 44/16 = 2.75 t CO2 per t CH4 and $\phi_{fl}$ the flared share
(CH4Inputs oil row `per_flare`). The fee raises revenue on the methane that remains:

$$
R^{mf}_t = MF_t \sum_j M_j(t)\, GWP_j\, \iota_j\ \frac{1000}{10^{6}}
$$ {#eq-em-mfrev}

where $R^{mf}$ is in USD million (`ch4.rev`), part of total revenue (@sec-fiscal).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: methane by source and the methane fee"}
```
# data step, once per country
for j in SOURCES:                                  # og, dg, cm, bm, liv, ric, wst
    A[j], B[j] = curve(country, j) or curve("AVG", j)          # 0 or missing: the average
    gwp[j] = GWPCH4F if j in FOSSIL else GWPCH4NF
    fee_on[j] = 1 if fee_switch[j] == "Yes" else 0
act0 = {og: prod0[oil] + prod0[gas], cm: prod0[coal], dg: cons0[gas], bm: cons0[bio], liv: 1, ric: 1, wst: 1}
for j in FOSSIL:
    w[j] = min(MethShareCap * act0[j] / sum(act0[i] for i in FOSSIL), share_input[j])
for j in SOURCES:
    pi[j] = w[j] / sum(w[i] for i in FOSSIL) if j in FOSSIL else (1 if j == wst else share_input[j])
    em0[j] = inv[Y][category(j), "ch4"] * pi[j] * 1000 / gwp[j]          # kt CH4

for t in years:
    mfee[t] = path(t, MPIntro, MPOutro, MPLevelStart, MPLevelTarget, continue_linear=True) * (scenario > 1) \
              + (cptraj[t] if CTforMethane == "Yes" else 0)
    for j in SOURCES:
        abt[j][t] = min(1, max(0, A[j] * (mfee[t] * gwp[j] * fee_on[j]) ** B[j]))
    for j in (og, cm):
        fk[j][t] = 0 if t == t0 else mfee[t] * gwp[j] * fee_on[j] * 1000 * em0[j] / act0[j] * (1 - abt[j][t])
    for f in (oil, gas, coal):
        pidx[f][t] = 1 if t == t0 else 1 + (fk[j(f)][t] - fk[j(f)][t-1]) / (gp_int[f][t] * units_per_ktoe[f]) * pass_through
        prd[f][t] = prod0[f] if t <= t0 + 1 else prd[f][t-1] * pidx[f][t] ** elast[f] * wd[f][t-1] / wd[f][t-2]
    act = {og: prd[oil][t] + prd[gas][t], cm: prd[coal][t], dg: ener["all", gas][t], bm: ener["all", bio][t]}
    for j in (liv, ric, wst):
        act[j] = 1 if t == t0 else act_prev[j] * (1 + gdppc_g[t]) ** el_inc[cat(j)] * (1 + pop_g[t]) ** el_pop[cat(j)]
    for j in SOURCES:
        intensity[j][t] = (1 - decline[j]) ** max(0, t - Y)
        ch4_em[j][t] = em0[j] * act[j] / act0[j] * intensity[j][t] * (1 - abt[j][t]) if act0[j] else 0
    ch4_sup[t] = sum(ch4_em[j][t] for j in FOSSIL)
    flr[t] = FlareCO2perCH4 * flared_share * em0[og] * act[og] / act0[og] * abt[og][t] / 1000     # Mt CO2
    ch4_rev[t] = mfee[t] * sum(ch4_em[j][t] * gwp[j] * fee_on[j] for j) * 1000 / 1e6           # USD m
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** methane fee rows `mfee.p`, `mfee` in section 1 (ScenarioDefinition `MPIntro`, `MPOutro`,
  `MPLevelStart`, `MPLevelTarget`, `CTforMethane`); section 14 rows `ghg.invb`, `ch4.src`, `ch4.wd`, `ch4.fk`,
  `ch4.pi`, `ch4.prd`, `ch4.act`, `ch4.abc`, `ch4.abt`, `ch4.int`, `ch4.em`, `ch4.sup`, `ghg.flr`, `ch4.rev`.
  Constants `MethShareCap`, `GWPCH4F`, `GWPCH4NF`, `FlareCO2perCH4`, `MethGJperKtoe`, `MethGJperBbl`,
  `MethGJperMMBtu`, `MethGJperT`. Manual inputs J185:J200.
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/policies.py`, `prepare()` (methane fee, EQ-M1.8);
  `ghg_data.py` (`inventory()`, `methane()`, `world_demand()`, `methane_inputs()`, `production()`) and
  `emissions.py`, `country_data()`, `curve_coefficient()` and `ghg()` (EQ-A7.3).
- **Fiscal space.** Since issue I47 was settled, the fiscal space of the GDP feedback counts the fee revenue on the
  scenario's own activity (`ch4.rev`), as legacy (row 8024). The memo rows `ch4.emf` and `ch4.revf` (the same sum
  with the stored scenario-1 activity for downstream gas and biomass, sheet BaselineCO2 rows `dg`, `bm`, check
  `ch4bs.chk` = 0 in scenario 1) are kept but no longer used. See @sec-fiscal.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT"}
- **L18, fixed.** Legacy holds non-energy methane constant and does not apply the abatement. Here livestock, rice
  and waste grow with income and population and the fee abates them (LD43).
- **L19, fixed.** Legacy counts the flaring CO2 as methane. Here it is energy CO2 (LD44).
- **L20, fixed.** Legacy's population growth path differs from UN WPP; the model uses UN WPP.
- **L21, fixed.** Legacy abates waste with the livestock curve. Each source uses its own curve.
- **L135, fixed.** Legacy applies the autonomous intensity decline to the energy sources only. Here livestock, rice
  and waste decline too. Legacy keeps the index at 1 up to 2023 and declines from 2024; the model declines from the
  last inventory year (I141).
- **I152, as legacy.** Where the country's curve coefficient is 0 or missing, the average curve is used (legacy
  Mitigation L6084:M6084).
- **LD46, as legacy.** The fee path applies only in policy scenarios; a switch per source decides where the fee
  applies, in the abatement and the revenue.
- **Production (I66).** Oil, gas and coal production follow legacy rows 6132-6149: world demand of the year before
  and the producer price response.
- **Methodology.** The methodology defines the fee per tonne of CH4 and describes the agriculture and waste
  "production" as also responding to oil producer prices; the model applies the fee per tonne of CO2e and the price
  response only to fossil fuel production.
:::

## Energy GHGs: combustion methane, N2O and F-gases {#sec-em-energy-ghg}

The energy category of the inventory holds CO2, methane, N2O and F-gases. CO2 comes from @sec-em-co2 plus
flaring. Methane combines combustion and fuel supply and is scaled to the inventory. N2O and F-gases follow simple
rules. The methodology describes these in
[methodology, sections 3.5.4.2 and 3.5.4.3](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#nitrous-oxide-n_2o-and-flourinated-gases-f-gases).

### Combustion methane {#sec-em-ch4comb}

Every fuel burnt emits some methane. The factor moves on a straight line from its base-year value towards its final
value in `EFEndYear`, and the line continues after that year, as legacy:

$$
w_t = \omega\ \frac{t - t_0}{T^{EF} - t_0}
$$ {#eq-em-efw}

$$
CH4_{s,f}(t) = F_{s,f}(t)\ \frac{e^{0}_{s,f} + (e^{1}_{s,f} - e^{0}_{s,f})\, w_t}{1000}, \qquad CH4_k(t) = PE_k(t)\ \frac{e^{0}_{k} + (e^{1}_{k} - e^{0}_{k})\, w_t}{1000}
$$ {#eq-em-ch4c}

where

- $w_t$ is the weight of the final factor, 0 in the base year;
- $\omega$ (`EFFinShare`) follows the factor selection `EFSel`: Constant 0, Variable 1, Average 0.5;
- $T^{EF}$ = 2039 (`EFEndYear`, the legacy column of the final factor; later years extrapolate the line);
- $e^{0}$, $e^{1}$ are the GAINS CH4 factors of the base year and the final year, t per ktoe, looked up as for the
  local pollutants (@sec-em-ap-data);
- $CH4_{s,f}$, $CH4_k$ are in kt CH4 (`ch4`); power uses the fuel input of the coal, gas, oil and biomass types.

The combustion methane of all subsectors and power is $CH4^{c}(t)$ (`ch4.c`), also reported by sector group.

### Energy methane, calibrated to the inventory {#sec-em-ch4enr}

Combustion plus supply methane, in CO2e, is scaled by one factor so that it equals the inventory in the last
inventory year:

$$
k_{CH_4} = \frac{M^{inv}_{enr,Y}}{\big(CH4^{c,B}_{Y} + M^{sup,B}_{Y}\big)\, GWP_F / 1000}
$$ {#eq-em-kch4}

$$
E_{enr,CH_4}(t) = k_{CH_4}\ \big(CH4^{c}(t) + M^{sup}(t)\big)\ \frac{GWP_F}{1000}
$$ {#eq-em-ch4enr}

where

- $k_{CH_4}$ is the calibration factor (`ghg.k`);
- $M^{inv}_{enr,Y}$ is the inventory energy methane in year $Y$ (Mt CO2e);
- $CH4^{c,B}_{Y}$, $M^{sup,B}_{Y}$ are the scenario-1 combustion and supply methane of year $Y$ (kt), stored as
  data (sheet BaselineCO2 rows `ch4c`, `ch4sup`, refreshed by the build), so that the factor, used in every year,
  reads no later model year (no circular reference);
- $GWP_F$ = 29.8, the fossil GWP;
- $E_{enr,CH_4}$ is energy methane in Mt CO2e.

Energy methane thus equals the inventory in $Y$ and then moves with fuel use, supply activity and abatement.

### Energy CO2, N2O and F-gases {#sec-em-enr-other}

$$
E_{enr,CO_2}(t) = em_{CO_2}(t) + CO2^{flr}_t
$$ {#eq-em-enrco2}

Energy CO2 is always the model's (fuel combustion, power included, plus flaring), also in inventory years. Energy
N2O and F-gases take the inventory while it has the year; after it, N2O moves with energy CO2 and F-gases are held:

$$
E_{enr,N_2O}(t) = E_{enr,N_2O}(t-1)\ \frac{em_{CO_2}(t)}{em_{CO_2}(t-1)}, \qquad E_{enr,F}(t) = E_{enr,F}(t-1)
$$ {#eq-em-enrn2o}

(the ratio is 1 if last year's CO2 is 0).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: energy GHGs"}
```
for t in years:
    w = EFFinShare * (t - t0) / (EFEndYear - t0)              # continues after EFEndYear
    for s, f: ch4[s, f][t] = ener[s, f][t] * (ef0_ch4[s, f] + (ef1_ch4[s, f] - ef0_ch4[s, f]) * w) / 1000
    for k in (coal, gas, oil, bio): ch4["pow", k][t] = pe[k][t] * (e0[k] + (e1[k] - e0[k]) * w) / 1000
    ch4_c[t] = sum(ch4[s, f][t]) + sum(ch4["pow", k][t])
    k_ch4 = inv[Y]["enr", "ch4"] / ((stored_ch4c_s1[Y] + stored_ch4sup_s1[Y]) * GWPCH4F / 1000)
    ghg["enr", "co2"][t] = co2_total[t] + flr[t]
    ghg["enr", "ch4"][t] = k_ch4 * (ch4_c[t] + ch4_sup[t]) * GWPCH4F / 1000
    if t in inventory:
        ghg["enr", "n2o"][t], ghg["enr", "fga"][t] = inv[t]["enr", "n2o"], inv[t]["enr", "fga"]
    else:
        ghg["enr", "n2o"][t] = ghg["enr", "n2o"][t-1] * (co2_total[t] / co2_total[t-1] if co2_total[t-1] else 1)
        ghg["enr", "fga"][t] = ghg["enr", "fga"][t-1]
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** combustion CH4 rows `ch4` of sections 5-8 (LAMBDA `NONCO2`, weight `EFWEIGHT`) and of section 14
  (power); `ch4.c`, `ghg.k`, `ghg` (energy rows) in section 14; stored values on sheet BaselineCO2; factors on sheet
  Inputs_nc (table by legacy EF code).
- **CPAT Python:** `fuel_use.py` (combustion CH4 of subsectors), `emissions.py`, `ghg()` (power CH4, `ch4.c`,
  `ghg.k`, energy rows; EQ-A7.2). The factor reads Excel-AI's stored scenario-1 values.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT"}
- **I34.** Legacy 465 has the CH4 factor lookups but leaves the factors blank, so its combustion methane is zero.
  The model fills them from GAINS (country, else World Bank region, else world).
- **Factor path (LD47, I98).** As legacy: linear from the base year to the final factor in 2039, continued after it.
  Only the base and final GAINS values are used: the yearly legacy paths are proprietary.
- **Methodology.** The methodology calibrates energy methane on 2019 and sets energy F-gases to zero after 2018.
  The model calibrates on the last inventory year and holds the inventory's last F-gas value.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: energy methane for Egypt"}
- Combustion methane exceeds inventory energy methane, so $k_{CH_4}$ is about 0.25 for Egypt.
- **Open issue I91.** Egypt's inventory breaks after 2021: energy CH4 is 21.9 Mt CO2e in 2021 and 1.9-2.0 in
  2022-2024, while the fugitive-emissions memo alone is 20.3 in 2023. Calibrating to 2024, as legacy, may understate
  energy methane by about 19 Mt CO2e.
- Oil, gas and coal production have no production model: they follow world demand from the base year.
:::

## Other inventory categories {#sec-em-other}

The non-energy categories take the inventory while it has the year. After that, each grows with its own driver:
industrial energy CO2 for industrial processes, income and population for agriculture, waste and other, an
exogenous decline for LULUCF. The methodology describes these in
[methodology, section 3.5.5](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#non-energy-related-emissions)
([A7.2](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A7-2), [M7.2](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M7-2)).

### Drivers {#sec-em-drivers}

$$
n_t = \frac{pop_t}{pop_{t-1}} - 1, \qquad g^{pc}_t = \frac{1 + g_t}{1 + n_t} - 1, \qquad
\psi_t = \begin{cases} em_{CO_2}(t) / em^{B}_{CO_2}(t) & \texttt{AdditionMitigationPoliciesNonEnergy} = \text{Yes} \\ 1 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-em-drivers}

where

- $pop_t$ is UN WPP population (thousands), $n_t$ its growth (`pop.g`);
- $g_t$ is real GDP growth after the GDP feedback (@sec-fiscal), $g^{pc}_t$ GDP per capita growth (`gdppc.g`);
- $\psi_t$ is the mitigation effort in non-energy sectors (`ghg.m`): the scenario's energy CO2 over the baseline's,
  if the scenario's switch is on. This option, in effect, extends the carbon price's effect to non-energy GHGs.

The growth factor of a category is

$$
d_{u,t} = (1 + g^{pc}_t)^{\epsilon^{Y}_u}\,(1 + n_t)^{\epsilon^{N}_u}\ \frac{\psi_t}{\psi_{t-1}}, \qquad d_{u,t_0} = 1
$$ {#eq-em-dr}

with the elasticities of sheet `Manual inputs` K325:M327, at the legacy addresses (a text entry such as "na" counts
as 0):

| Category $u$ | Income elasticity $\epsilon^{Y}$ (row 327) | Population elasticity $\epsilon^{N}$ (row 326) |
|---|---|---|
| Agriculture | 0.15 | 0.9 |
| Waste | 0 ("na") | 1 |
| Other | 0 ("na") | 1 |

These values reproduce the cached results of the legacy run exactly. Legacy Mitigation uses the same values; it
never reads the manual cells, whose formula is broken (`#REF!`).

### Projection by category and gas {#sec-em-categories}

Each category $u$ and gas $p$ takes the inventory value while the inventory has the year:

$$
E_{u,p}(t) = \begin{cases} \text{inventory}_{u,p,t} & t \le Y \\ \text{projection of the table below} & t > Y \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-em-ghg}

(energy CO2 and energy methane excepted: they are always modelled, @sec-em-energy-ghg).

| Category and gas | Projection after the inventory |
|---|---|
| Industrial processes, all gases | $E(t-1)\,(1 + \Delta_t)$ with $\Delta_t$ the growth of industrial energy CO2 (`ghg.gi`), if `IndustrialProcessEmissionsScaleEner` = Yes; else held |
| Agriculture CO2, N2O, F-gases | $E(t-1)\, d_{agr,t}$ |
| Agriculture CH4 | livestock and rice methane: $(M_{liv} + M_{ric})\, GWP_{NF} / 1000$ |
| Waste CO2, N2O, F-gases | $E(t-1)\, d_{wst,t}$ |
| Waste CH4 | waste methane: $M_{wst}\, GWP_{NF} / 1000$ |
| Other, all gases | $E(t-1)\, d_{oth,t}$ |
| LULUCF CO2 | @eq-em-lulucf |
| LULUCF CH4, N2O, F-gases | held |

The industrial growth may be negative: process emissions decline with industrial CO2, as legacy rows 7553 and
7566-7569.

LULUCF CO2 declines by a share of the last inventory value while it is a source, and is held while it is a sink:

$$
E_{lucf,CO_2}(t) = \begin{cases}
E_{lucf,CO_2}(t-1) & E_{lucf,CO_2}(t-1) < 0 \\
E_{lucf,CO_2}(t-1)\ \dfrac{\psi_t}{\psi_{t-1}} - \delta_{lu}\, \big|E^{inv}_{lucf,CO_2,Y}\big| & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-em-lulucf}

where $\delta_{lu}$ is `LULUCFAnnualEmissionsDecline` (ScenarioDefinition, share per year of the last inventory
value; the methodology's default is 2.5%) and $E^{inv}_{lucf,CO_2,Y}$ the inventory value of year $Y$.

### Totals {#sec-em-totals}

$$
GHG_t = \sum_{u \ne \text{LULUCF}} \sum_{p} E_{u,p}(t), \qquad GHG^{inc}_t = GHG_t + \sum_p E_{lucf,p}(t)
$$ {#eq-em-ghgtot}

The block reports totals by gas and by category, GHG emissions excluding (`ghg`) and including LULUCF (`ghg.inc`),
the baseline value (`ghg.ref`) and the change against it (`ghg.pct`, `ghg.chg`).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: other inventory categories"}
```
for t in years:
    pop_g[t] = pop[t] / pop[t-1] - 1
    gdppc_g[t] = (1 + gdp_growth[t]) / (1 + pop_g[t]) - 1
    m[t] = co2_total[t] / co2_ref[t] if AdditionMitigationPoliciesNonEnergy == "Yes" and co2_ref[t] > 0 else 1
    gi[t] = 0 if t == t0 else co2["ind"][t] / co2["ind"][t-1] - 1      # 0 if last year's is 0
    for u in (agr, wst, oth):
        dr[u][t] = 1 if t == t0 else (1 + gdppc_g[t]) ** el_inc[u] * (1 + pop_g[t]) ** el_pop[u] * m[t] / m[t-1]
    for u in (ipr, agr, lucf, wst, oth):
        for p in (co2, ch4, n2o, fga):
            if t in inventory: ghg[u, p][t] = inv[t][u, p]; continue
            prev = ghg[u, p][t-1]
            if u == ipr:   ghg[u, p][t] = prev * (1 + (gi[t] if IndustrialProcessEmissionsScaleEner == "Yes" else 0))
            elif (u, p) == (agr, ch4): ghg[u, p][t] = (ch4_em[liv][t] + ch4_em[ric][t]) * GWPCH4NF / 1000
            elif (u, p) == (wst, ch4): ghg[u, p][t] = ch4_em[wst][t] * GWPCH4NF / 1000
            elif (u, p) == (lucf, co2):
                ghg[u, p][t] = prev if prev < 0 else prev / m[t-1] * m[t] - abs(inv[Y][lucf, co2]) * LULUCFAnnualEmissionsDecline
            elif u == lucf: ghg[u, p][t] = prev
            else:          ghg[u, p][t] = prev * dr[u][t]
    ghg_total[t] = sum(ghg[u, p][t] for u != lucf, p)
    ghg_inc[t] = ghg_total[t] + sum(ghg[lucf, p][t] for p)
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** section 14 rows `pop`, `pop.g`, `gdppc.g`, `ghg.h` (row of the year on sheet GHGs, 0 if none),
  `ghg.m`, `ghg.gi`, `ghg.dr`, `ghg`, `ghg.inc`, `ghg.ref`, `ghg.pct`, `ghg.chg`. ScenarioDefinition
  `AdditionMitigationPoliciesNonEnergy`, `IndustrialProcessEmissionsScaleEner`, `LULUCFAnnualEmissionsDecline`;
  elasticities Manual inputs K325:M327 (names `GhgElCat`, `GhgElPop`, `GhgElInc`).
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/ghg_data.py`, `inventory()`, `population()`,
  `nonenergy_elasticities()`; `emissions.py`, `ghg()` (EQ-M7.2, EQ-A7.2).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT and the methodology"}
- **Industrial processes.** The model lets process emissions decline with industrial CO2 in every year (as legacy
  rows 7553, 7566-7569). The methodology floors the growth at 0 in its first projection year only.
- **LULUCF.** The model holds sinks (negative values) and holds LULUCF CH4, N2O and F-gases. The methodology also
  subtracts the annual decline from sinks, scales CH4 and N2O by the effort and grows N2O and F-gases with
  population.
- **Population (L20).** UN WPP population, not legacy's growth path.
- **Validation.** When the block was introduced, every earlier output was unchanged (the methane fee is 0 in the
  shipped scenarios). The check recomputes every GHG and combustion-methane row in Python from the data files
  (scenarios 1 and 2, every year). Sheet LegacyDiff lists the remaining differences.
:::

## NDC comparison {#sec-em-ndc}

The NDC rows translate the country's nationally determined contribution into a target for GHG emissions including
LULUCF and measure how far each scenario goes towards it. They compare only: there is no goal seek on the NDC (user
decision). The methodology describes the NDC types in
[methodology, section 3.5.6](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#national-determined-contributions),
with worked examples in
[Appendix D](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#sec-AppendixD)
([A7.4](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A7-4)).

### Data and choices {#sec-em-ndc-data}

| Sheet | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| NDCs | NDC table by country and round (latest, second, first): type, target years, reference year, unconditional and conditional values, LULUCF and gas coverage; key ISO \| round | Legacy NDCs rows 48-242 (latest), 250-444 (second), 451-644 (first), columns C-P |
| GHGHist | Historical GHGs excluding and including LULUCF, CO2 excluding LULUCF, energy CO2, by year; key group \| year | Legacy GHGs rows 954-1189 |

Three choices, read from scenario 1 as legacy:

| Input | Options |
|---|---|
| `NDCs` | First round, Second round, else the latest (`Latest*`) |
| `NDCTargetYear` | `Main*` = the first target year; otherwise the second, where given |
| `Conditionality` | Unconditional, Conditional, else the average of the two |

The target year is at most 2035 (`NDCYrCap`): later targets are compared in that year. A country without an NDC row
is Unquantifiable.

### Target level {#sec-em-ndc-target}

The target is first built on the NDC's own basis (gases CO2 or GHGs; LULUCF included or excluded), against the
modelled BAU $B_{ty}$: scenario 1 on that basis in the target year $ty$. With $x$ the target value as given
(a reduction is negative; Fixed targets in Mt CO2e), the level $\ell$ is:

| Type | Target level $\ell$ |
|---|---|
| BAU | $B_{ty}\,(1 + x)$ |
| Fixed | $x$ |
| Historical | $H\,(1 + x)$, with $H$ the emissions of the reference year |
| Intensity | $H\ \dfrac{GDP_{ty}}{GDP_{ref}}\ (1 + x)$, real GDP of WEO |
| Unquantifiable | $B_{ty}$ |

$H$ is scenario 1 when the reference year is modelled (from the base year), else the GHGs inventory (2021-2024,
rows `ndc.hc`, `ndc.hv`), else GHGHist. The reduction against the BAU and the target in GHGs including LULUCF are

$$
r = 1 - \frac{\ell}{B_{ty}}, \qquad L^{NDC} = \min\!\big(B^{inc}_{ty},\ B^{inc}_{ty}\,(1 - r)\big)
$$ {#eq-em-ndcr}

where

- $r$ is computed for the unconditional ($u$) and conditional ($c$) values; $r_a$ is their average (the one given if
  only one; 0 if none); $r_{sel}$ is the `Conditionality` choice ($r_a$ if the chosen one is not given);
- $B^{inc}_{ty}$ is scenario-1 GHGs including LULUCF in the target year;
- $L^{NDC}$ is the target (`ndc.lvl`), for $u$, $c$ and $sel$, as legacy rows 18494-18496.

### Progress against the NDC {#sec-em-ndc-gap}

For every scenario and year:

$$
red_t = 1 - \frac{GHG^{inc}_t}{GHG^{inc,B}_t}, \qquad gap_t = \frac{red_t}{r_{sel}}, \qquad over_t = GHG^{inc}_t - L^{NDC}_{sel}
$$ {#eq-em-ndcgap}

where

- $red_t$ is the reduction of GHGs including LULUCF against scenario 1 (`ndc.red`);
- $gap_t$ is the share of the NDC reduction achieved (`ndc.gap`, legacy "Gap to NDC"; 1 if no reduction is
  required);
- $over_t$ is the excess over the chosen target (`ndc.over`); in the target year it is the legacy goal-seek
  difference (G18501).

The rows also give the target against base-year GHGs including LULUCF (`ndc.idx`).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: NDC comparison (after the year loop)"}
```
row = ndc_table[country, round(NDCs)]                       # None: Unquantifiable
alt = NDCTargetYear != "Main*" and row.ty2 > 0
ty = min(NDCYrCap, row.ty2 if alt else row.ty1)
basis = ghg_co2 (+ lulucf_co2 if LULUCF included) if gases == "CO2" else (ghg_inc if LULUCF included else ghg)
B_ty, Binc_ty = basis_s1[ty], ghg_inc_s1[ty]
H = basis_s1[ref] if ref modelled else inventory[ref] if ref in 2021..2024 else ghghist[ref]
for v in (u, c):
    f = 1 + x[v]                                            # N/A if not given
    level[v] = {BAU: B_ty*f, Fixed: f-1, Historical: H*f, Intensity: H*gdp[ty]/gdp[ref]*f, Unq: B_ty}[type]
    r[v] = 1 - level[v] / B_ty
r[a] = mean of the given r[u], r[c] (0 if none)
r[sel] = r[Conditionality] if given else r[a]
for v in (u, c, sel): target[v] = min(Binc_ty, Binc_ty * (1 - r[v]))
for t in years:
    red[t] = 1 - ghg_inc[t] / ghg_inc_s1[t]
    gap[t] = red[t] / r[sel] if r[sel] > 0 else 1
    over[t] = ghg_inc[t] - target[sel]
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** section 14 NDC rows (`ndc.key` to `ndc.over`); sheets NDCs and GHGHist, both built by
  `extract_legacy_tables.py ndc`; choices on ScenarioDefinition scenario 1 (`NDCs`, `NDCTargetYear`,
  `Conditionality`); constant `NDCYrCap`.
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/emissions.py`, `ndc()` (EQ-A7.4), in the finish blocks of `chain.py`.
  Text rows and N/A are not compared numerically (N/A is NaN).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT"}
Legacy F12 rows 18403-18518. Bugs fixed:

- **L119.** Legacy applies the year adjustment twice for BAU targets and never for Fixed or Historical. The model
  compares in the target year.
- **L120.** Legacy's index rows invert the unconditional and conditional ratios against the average.
- **L121.** For Historical targets legacy takes the cut as the target "level".
- **L122.** Intensity targets including LULUCF add a blank cell instead of LULUCF emissions.
- **L123.** Intensity targets read the reference-year GDP from a fixed cell.

Issues: **L169**, China's CO2 is hard-coded in legacy (not replicated); **I95**, reference years outside the data
give N/A. The 2021-2024 inventory now covers some of them; 2018-2020 need data.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: Egypt's NDC"}
Latest NDC: BAU type, 2030, −27% unconditional, GHGs excluding LULUCF. Target 344.3 Mt CO2e (legacy 355.7 = its
BAU 487.2 $\times$ 0.73; the model's BAU is 471.7, the known baseline GHG difference). Scenario 2 achieves 21% of
the required reduction in 2030 (legacy 51% for its cached policy scenario, which is not the model's scenario 2).
:::

## Local air pollutants {#sec-em-ap}

The model computes seven local air pollutants from the fuel use of every subsector and of power generation: fine
particulate matter (PM2.5), nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulphur dioxide (SO2), volatile organic compounds (VOC), black
carbon (BC), organic carbon (OC) and carbon monoxide (CO). They are not part of the GHG totals; a memo converts them
to CO2 equivalents. They are also grouped into the sectors of the air-pollution module, which reads them. The
methodology describes the emissions in
[methodology, sections 6.4.2 and 6.4.3](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/06_Air_pollution.html#emission-factors-from-gains)
([A7.6](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A7-6)).

Units: emissions in kt; factors in t per ktoe; forcing in Mt CO2e (GWP100).

### Data and factor lookup {#sec-em-ap-data}

| Sheet | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| EF_NonCO2 | Combustion factors by country or World Bank region, GAINS subsector, fuel and pollutant, base year and final, kt per PJ | Legacy sheet EF_PM (GAINS, all countries and regions); also used for combustion CH4 |
| GWP_AP | GWP100 of the pollutants by GAINS region | Legacy GWP table of the pollutant forcing |
| Countries (column O) | GAINS region of every country (Egypt: `afr`) | Legacy Countries tab |

The factors are those of legacy 465 (Mitigation rows 1052-1663), in a table by legacy EF code. Each factor is chosen
in three steps:

1. **EF subsector.** Road, rail, aviation (jet fuel), residential, services, construction, other manufacturing, food
   & forestry and other energy keep their own code. Mining & chemicals, iron & steel, other metals, machinery,
   cement and fuel transformation take manufacturing (`mnf`, legacy rows 6388-6395). Navigation, which legacy leaves
   out (bug L22), takes its own GAINS code `nav`.
2. **Country, region, world.** The factor of the country (`egy.mit.ef.<sub>.<fuel>.<pollutant>`), else of its World
   Bank region (`CtryReg`, Egypt `mea`), else of the world (`wld`, absent from the data), else 0. The kt per PJ values
   are converted to t per ktoe (factor 41.868).
3. **Other energy** (`oen`) takes, for each fuel and pollutant, the maximum factor across the other legacy
   subsectors (power included), as the legacy note says (issue I147).

Only the fuel and subsector pairs of the legacy table have factors: power (coal, gas, oil, biomass); road (gasoline,
diesel, LPG, kerosene, gas); rail (diesel); aviation (jet fuel); residential (no gasoline or diesel). A pair or
pollutant with no factor in the chain gives 0, as legacy: for example power biomass, road kerosene, residential oil,
construction coal, gas, oil and biomass, services and other manufacturing coal, organic carbon and SO2 of LPG. None
of these pairs burns fuel in Egypt.

### Emissions and totals {#sec-em-ap-method}

The factor path is that of combustion methane (@eq-em-efw). Emissions are fuel use times the weighted factor,
summed over fuels:

$$
AP_{p,s}(t) = \sum_f F_{s,f}(t)\ \frac{(1 - w_t)\, e^{0}_{p,s,f} + w_t\, e^{1}_{p,s,f}}{1000}, \qquad
AP_{p,pow}(t) = \sum_k PE_k(t)\ \frac{(1 - w_t)\, e^{0}_{p,k} + w_t\, e^{1}_{p,k}}{1000}
$$ {#eq-em-ap}

where

- $AP_{p,s}$ is the emission of pollutant $p$ by subsector $s$ (kt), `ap`;
- $e^{0}$, $e^{1}$ are the base-year and final factors (t per ktoe);
- fuel use is the modelled one, so prices, policies and scenarios carry through.

Transport, buildings and industry sum their subsectors, navigation included. A pollutant's total is all subsectors
plus power: $AP_p = \sum_s AP_{p,s} + AP_{p,pow}$.

The **forcing memo** converts the emissions with the GWP100 of the country's GAINS region:

$$
F^{ap}_p = AP_p\ GWP_{p,r} / 1000, \qquad F^{ap} = \sum_{p \in \{BC, OC, NOx, SO2, VOC, CO\}} F^{ap}_p
$$ {#eq-em-apf}

in Mt CO2e (`apf`). Cooling pollutants (OC, SO2, NOx) have a negative GWP, so the net forcing can be negative.
Energy GHGs including the forcing are $E_{enr} + F^{ap}$ (`ghg.enrp`, legacy "Total GHGs and PM", rows 18310 and
18321).

### Sectors of the air-pollution module {#sec-em-ap-sectors}

The air-pollution module reads the emissions grouped in seven sectors, which add up to each pollutant's total:

| Module sector | Content |
|---|---|
| coal power plants | fuel use of the coal type $\times$ the power factors |
| gas power plants | fuel use of the gas type $\times$ the power factors |
| other power plants | power less coal and gas plants |
| ground level road | road |
| ground level other | residential, services, construction |
| other | rail, aviation, navigation, industry without construction, other energy use |
| food & forestry | food & forestry |

In each sector, primary organic matter and the rest of PM2.5 are derived:

$$
POM = 1.3\ OC, \qquad PM^{oth} = \max(0,\ PM2.5 - BC - POM)
$$ {#eq-em-pom}

The table follows the layout of the legacy input table (Mitigation rows 15859-15961): one block per module sector
and one for all sectors; in each, ten pollutants in legacy order: NOx, SO2, BC, POM, other PM2.5, VOC, CH4, CO, PM2.5,
OC; codes `aps.<pollutant>.<sector>`, in kt (legacy: tonnes). The module reads these rows directly. Methane in the
table, as legacy (issue I34):

| Module sector | CH4 |
|---|---|
| coal, gas, other power plants | combustion CH4 of the generation types |
| road, ground level other | combustion CH4 of their subsectors |
| other | combustion CH4 of its subsectors plus fuel-supply methane (legacy: oil and gas extraction only) |
| food & forestry | combustion CH4 plus livestock, rice and waste methane |

This methane is not calibrated: it is not scaled by $k_{CH_4}$.

Food & forestry is also split into food and forestry/agriculture, as legacy (LD53): the food share of each fuel is
`info_food` over the four `info_` flows of the processed Balances (legacy rows 501-504, 1666-1673). Rows `apfd` (food
fuel use) and `ap.<pollutant>.fod`, `.fag` are memo rows, not in the totals. The share is 0 for Egypt. The module also
reads power and residential fuel use (`apen`) and energy CO2 (`apco2`).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: local air pollutants"}
```
for t in years:
    w = EFFinShare * (t - t0) / (EFEndYear - t0)
    for p in (pm2, nox, so2, voc, bc, oc, co):
        for s in subsectors:
            ap[p, s][t] = sum(ener[s, f][t] * ((1 - w) * e0[p, s, f] + w * e1[p, s, f]) / 1000 for f in fuels)
        ap[p, "pow"][t] = sum(pe[k][t] * ((1 - w) * e0[p, k] + w * e1[p, k]) / 1000 for k in gen_types)
        ap[p, "all"][t] = sum(ap[p, s][t] for s) + ap[p, "pow"][t]
    for p in (bc, oc, nox, so2, voc, co):
        apf[p][t] = ap[p, "all"][t] * gwp100[gains_region, p] / 1000
    ghg_enrp[t] = ghg["enr", "all"][t] + sum(apf[p][t] for p)
    for p in (nox, so2, bc, voc, co, pm2, oc):
        aps["cpp", p] = pe[coal] * ef_pow(coal, p, w);   aps["gpp", p] = pe[gas] * ef_pow(gas, p, w)
        aps["opp", p] = ap[p, "pow"] - aps["cpp", p] - aps["gpp", p]
        aps["rod", p] = ap[p, rod];   aps["gro", p] = ap[p, res] + ap[p, srv] + ap[p, cst]
        aps["oth", p] = sum(ap[p, s] for s in (ral, avi, nav, mch, irn, nfm, mac, cem, omn, ftr, oen))
        aps["foo", p] = ap[p, foo]
    for m in module_sectors:
        aps[m, "pom"] = PomPerOC * aps[m, "oc"]
        aps[m, "opm"] = max(0, aps[m, "pm2"] - aps[m, "bc"] - aps[m, "pom"])
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** section 15 rows `ap.w`, `apfd`, `ap`, `apf`, `aps`, `apen`, `apco2`; `ghg.enrp` in section 14b;
  factor table on sheet Inputs_nc (Inputs, merged view); constants `EFEndYear`, `PomPerOC`, `EFtPerKtoe`. MTOutputs
  reports total PM2.5, NOx, SO2, black carbon and the forcing for every scenario; the Charts sheet plots PM2.5 and
  SO2.
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/ef_data.py`, `nonco2_efs()` and `region()` (EQ-A7.1);
  `emissions.py`, `pollutants()` and `gwp_region()` (EQ-A7.6).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT"}
- **L22, fixed.** Legacy omits navigation from the pollutant totals. It is included here.
- **L23, fixed.** Legacy leaves services and food & forestry out of each pollutant's total, although its
  air-pollution sectors include them. Here the total is the sum of the sectors.
- **L58, L59.** Subsectors and fuels without a GAINS factor got zero factors in legacy; the CPAT team fixed both in
  465 (country, else region, else world). The model follows 465 and keeps 0 where the 465 chain has no factor, as no
  such pair burns fuel in Egypt. Egypt 2022: food & forestry diesel, residential and fuel-transformation LPG,
  other-manufacturing diesel and LPG take the Middle East & North Africa factors, as legacy.
- **I147.** Other energy takes the maximum factor of the fuel across the other subsectors. Legacy takes the maximum
  year by year; the model the maximum of the base and of the final factors, with the line between them. The two agree
  where one subsector holds the maximum throughout (Egypt: other oil products, the only fuel of other energy).
- **Factor paths.** Legacy reads factor paths by year, which are proprietary and empty in the NoPropData file. The
  model draws a line between the base and final factors (as for CH4).
- **NH3.** Legacy has no ammonia from fuel combustion, so neither does the model.
- **Not built.** The health part of the air-pollution module that uses these sectors.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: results for Egypt (scenario 1)"}
- In 2022 every module sector equals the legacy input table (rows 15844-16053, tonnes) for every pollutant, except
  "other", which adds navigation (L22: NOx +14.8 kt, SO2 +13.7 kt, BC +0.6 kt, PM2.5 +1.5 kt), and CH4 (combustion
  CH4 and all fuel-supply methane, I34).
- Gas power plants' NOx is 96,931 t, road NOx 557,470 t, food & forestry black carbon 3.8 t, in both.
- Modelled ambient PM2.5 in 2022 is 33.06 µg/m3 against legacy 30.17; the difference is navigation's (2.89).
- In 2030 the sectors differ from legacy by the fuel-use paths (gas plants 0.88, other plants 0.62, road
  0.70-0.77, food & forestry 0.58 of legacy), not by the factors.
- The net forcing is about −17.5 Mt CO2e in 2022.
- The check recomputes all rows of the block in Python for scenarios 1 and 2.
:::

## Changes against the baseline, grid intensity and the Kaya identity {#sec-em-results}

A few result rows summarise the emissions of each scenario: the change against scenario 1, the carbon intensity of
the grid and a Kaya decomposition of CO2.

### CO2 and GHG change {#sec-em-change}

$$
\Delta em_{CO_2,x}(t) = em_{CO_2,x}(t) - em^{B}_{CO_2,x}(t), \qquad \Delta E_{x}(t) = E_{x}(t) - E^{B}_{x}(t)
$$ {#eq-em-chg}

`cchg` is the change of CO2 from fuel combustion by fuel and by sector group, power included (Mt CO2). `gchg` is the
change of GHGs by inventory category (energy, industrial processes, agriculture, LULUCF, waste, other) and by gas
(Mt CO2e). Legacy's "GHG by broad sector" (rows 18229-18243) is the inventory categories, so no allocation of CH4
and N2O to sectors is needed.

### Grid emission intensity {#sec-em-grid}

$$
EI^{grid}_t = \frac{em_{pow,CO_2}(t) \cdot 10^{6}}{G^{tot}_t \cdot H}
$$ {#eq-em-grid}

where $EI^{grid}$ is in t CO2 per MWh (`co2.grid`, 0 if there is no generation), $G^{tot}$ total generation in MW
years (@sec-power) and $H$ = 8760 hours per year. Egypt: 0.41 in 2022 (legacy 0.38) and 0.33 in 2030.

### Kaya identity {#sec-em-kaya}

The Kaya identity splits CO2 into population, income, energy intensity and carbon intensity:

$$
CO2 = POP \times \frac{GDP}{POP} \times \frac{TPES}{GDP} \times \frac{CO2}{TPES}
$$ {#eq-em-kaya}

| Row | Content | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `kaya.pop` | Population | million |
| `kaya.gpc` | GDP per capita: baseline real GDP (the header row, in every scenario) / population | thousand USD |
| `kaya.tpes` | Total primary energy supply | ktoe |
| `kaya.ei` | Energy intensity: TPES / GDP | ktoe per USD bn |
| `kaya.ci` | Carbon intensity: total CO2 including industrial processes (`ghg` CO2) $\times$ 1000 / TPES | kt CO2 per ktoe |

Total primary energy supply is the fuel use of all sectors (fuels burnt in power plants and biomass included) plus
primary electricity, the energy input of nuclear, wind, solar, hydro and other renewables:

$$
TPES_t = \sum_{s,f} F_{s,f}(t) + \sum_{k \in \{nuc, wnd, sol, hyd, orn\}} PE_k(t)
$$ {#eq-em-tpes}

The input of a primary type is its generation divided by its efficiency (physical energy content method: nuclear at
38%, renewables at about 1). Each factor is also indexed to the base year of the scenario (`kidx`: population, GDP,
GDP per capita, energy intensity, carbon intensity, CO2). The check `kidx.chk`, the product of the four factors,
equals the CO2 index exactly. Ratios use `SAFEDIV` (0 when the divisor is 0).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: result rows"}
```
for t in years:
    for x in fuels + sector_groups + ["pow"]:
        cchg[x][t] = co2[x][t] - co2_baseline[x][t]
    for u in categories:  gchg[u][t] = ghg[u, "all"][t] - ghg_baseline[u, "all"][t]
    for p in gases:       gchg[p][t] = ghg["all", p][t] - ghg_baseline["all", p][t]
    co2_grid[t] = safediv(co2["pow"][t] * 1e6, gtot[t] * 8760)
    kaya_pop[t]  = pop[t] / 1000
    kaya_gpc[t]  = safediv(gdp_usd[t], kaya_pop[t])
    kaya_tpes[t] = ener["all", "all"][t] + sum(pe[k][t] for k in (nuc, wnd, sol, hyd, orn))
    kaya_ei[t]   = safediv(kaya_tpes[t], gdp_usd[t])
    kaya_ci[t]   = safediv(ghg["all", "co2"][t] * 1000, kaya_tpes[t])
    for x in (pop, gdp, gpc, ei, ci, co2): kidx[x][t] = safediv(level[x][t], level[x][t0])
    kidx_chk[t] = kidx[pop][t] * kidx[gpc][t] * kidx[ei][t] * kidx[ci][t]      # = kidx[co2][t]
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** section 13 rows `cchg`, `co2.grid`, `kaya`, `kidx`, `co2.chg` (13b); section 14 rows `gchg`,
  `ghg.enrp` (14b). LAMBDA `SAFEDIV`.
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/emissions.py`, `co2()` (`cchg`, `co2.grid`), `ghg()` (`gchg`), `kaya()`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT"}
- Kaya identity as legacy (rows 18877-18893). An earlier version used fuel use only for TPES (2.6% lower in 2022);
  it was corrected to include primary electricity at the user's request. Legacy's broken "simplified Kaya" row
  (18931, −97%) is a different row and is not used.
- The efficiencies of wind (1.004), solar (1.026) and hydro (0.937) are legacy's power data, kept (issue I93).
- Population is the UN series, 111.7 million in 2022 against legacy's 103.6 million (bug L20, fixed). GDP per capita
  is therefore lower than in legacy; the identity still holds.
- Grid intensity: legacy Mitigation row 6582.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: Kaya identity for Egypt"}
- TPES 2022: 89,471 ktoe = legacy 89,471. Energy intensity 163.57 ktoe per USD bn = legacy.
- 2030, baseline: CO2 $\times$ 1.17, with energy intensity 0.81 and carbon intensity 1.03.
- 2030, carbon tax: energy intensity 0.74, CO2 $\times$ 1.10.
:::

## The new emissions trading system {#sec-em-ets}

A new ETS caps the CO2 of the sectors it covers. The model does not solve for the market price inside the year
loop. It sets a permit price from the cap with a closed-form estimate, lets that price act on fuel use like a carbon
tax (for the auctioned part) or like a feebate (for the part allocated free), and then reports how close covered
emissions come to the cap, with the price that would close the gap. The methodology treats the new ETS price with
the carbon prices in
[methodology, section 3.2.4](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#sec-PricesForecastedYears) and its
goal seek in [section 3.9.3.5](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#new-price-target-goal-seek); the
user guide in [section 1.3.2.4.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/01_User_Guide.html#emission-trading-systems).

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  I["Cap, coverage,<br/>benchmarks, volatility"] --> E["Fast estimate<br/>(or override)"]
  E --> P["Permit price p,<br/>tax-equivalent p·V"]
  P --> W["Auctioned part:<br/>price wedge"]
  P --> S["Free part:<br/>shadow price"]
  W --> U["Fuel use, CO2"]
  S --> U
  U --> K["Covered vs cap,<br/>next price"]
  K -. "goal seek" .-> E
```

### Inputs {#sec-em-ets-inputs}

| Input | Notes |
|---|---|
| Apply new ETS (`NewETS`); start year `ETSIntro`, target year `ETSOutro` | ScenarioDefinition |
| Cap change against baseline covered emissions at start and target (`ETSChangeRelStart`, `ETSChangeRelTarget`); continuation (`ETSCapCont`) | `Constant` keeps the cap level after the target year; any other value keeps the relative change |
| Price override switch (`ETSPriceOverride`) | `Yes`: the permit price comes from the override row of prices |
| Volatility (`ETSVolatility`), impact of volatility (`ETSVolImpact`), carbon tax policy risk (`ETSCTRisk`) | Labels Medium, High, Low, Zero; values from legacy sheet ETS+LTS |
| Sector coverage (`etscov`) | 17 ETS sectors: power and the 16 subsectors |
| Auctioned proportion at start and target (`ETSAuctStart`, `ETSAuctTarget`) | ScenarioDefinition rows 90-91; benchmark = 1 − auctioned proportion |
| Semi-elasticities by ETS sector | Legacy ETS+LTS table by country and sector group (sheet ETSSemi); used only by the fast estimate |
| Baseline CO2 by ETS sector | Scenario-1 CO2 by ETS sector, stored as data and refreshed by the build (check `bco2.chk` = 0) |
| Effectiveness of output-based allocation $\vartheta$; convergence exponent $\beta$ | Settings C14 and C15: 0.5 and 0.5 (legacy hardcodes) |

The volatility labels map to values as follows:

| Label | Medium | High | Low | Zero |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Annual price volatility $vol$ | 0.42 | 0.63 | 0.28 | 0 |
| Abatement cost increase per unit of volatility $imp$ | 0.5 | 0.75 | 0.333 | 0 |

The sector groups of the ETS benchmarks are power, transport (road, rail, aviation, navigation), residential
(residential, food & forestry, services) and industry (the industrial subsectors and other energy use). The
semi-elasticity groups are the same, except that food & forestry and services use the industry value. Egypt's
semi-elasticities, per USD per t CO2: power −0.00279, transport −0.00283, residential −0.00386, industry −0.00549.

### Coverage, benchmarks and the cap {#sec-em-ets-cap}

The ETS is on from its start year, and a sector counts once it is covered and the ETS is on
([M1.3](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-3)):

$$
on_t = \mathbb{1}[\texttt{NewETS} = \text{Yes and } t \ge T^{E}_0], \qquad \kappa_{e,t} = on_t\ \mathbb{1}[\text{sector } e \text{ covered}]
$$ {#eq-em-etson}

The benchmark is the share of a sector's emission intensity allocated free. It runs linearly from the start to the
target year and is flat after; the output-based (OBR) share of a sector is its group's benchmark, bounded to 0-1:

$$
b_{G,t} = \bar\Lambda\big(t;\, T^{E}_0, T^{E}_1,\, 1 - \alpha_0,\, 1 - \alpha_1\big), \qquad \omega_{e,t} = \min\!\big(1, \max(0, b_{G(e),t})\big)
$$ {#eq-em-obr}

where

- $b_{G,t}$ is the benchmark of group $G$ (`etsb`), 0 before the start year;
- $\bar\Lambda$ is the linear path held flat after the target year (@sec-model-overview);
- $\alpha_0$, $\alpha_1$ are the auctioned proportions at the start and target year, the same for every group, as
  legacy (issue I21). The default is $\alpha = 0$: nothing auctioned, benchmark 1, as legacy;
- $\omega_{e,t}$ is the OBR share (`obr`); the auctioned share is $1 - \omega_{e,t}$.

The cap is a change against baseline covered emissions:

$$
bce_t = \sum_e CO2^{B}_{e,t}\ \kappa_{e,t}, \qquad chg_t = \bar\Lambda\big(t;\, T^{E}_0, T^{E}_1, chg_0, chg_1\big)
$$ {#eq-em-bce}

$$
cap_t = \begin{cases}
on_t\ cap_{t-1} & t > T^{E}_1 \text{ and } \texttt{ETSCapCont} = \text{Constant} \\
on_t\ bce_t\,(1 + chg_t) & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-em-cap}

where

- $CO2^{B}_{e,t}$ is the stored scenario-1 CO2 of ETS sector $e$ (`bco2`, Mt), $bce_t$ baseline covered emissions
  (`ets.bce`);
- $chg_t$ is the cap change (`ets.chg`, negative for a cut), held at $chg_1$ after the target year, so that "any
  other" continuation keeps the relative change;
- $cap_t$ is the cap (`ets.cap`, Mt).

### Fast price estimate and the permit price {#sec-em-ets-price}

Price volatility makes an ETS less effective than a tax at the same price. The model expresses this as a volatility
adjustment, the tax-equivalent value of one dollar of permit price:

$$
V = \frac{1 + risk \cdot imp}{1 + vol \cdot imp}
$$ {#eq-em-vadj}

where $V$ is `ets.vadj`, $risk$ the carbon tax policy risk and $vol$, $imp$ the values of the labels above. At
Medium: $(1 + 0.2 \times 0.5)/(1 + 0.42 \times 0.5) = 1/1.1$.

The covered semi-elasticity weights each covered sector's semi-elasticity by its baseline emissions and discounts the
free part by the effectiveness of output-based allocation:

$$
\bar\sigma_t = \frac{\sum_e CO2^{B}_{e,t}\ \kappa_{e,t}\ \sigma_e\ \big(1 - (1 - \vartheta)\,\omega_{e,t}\big)}{bce_t}
$$ {#eq-em-se}

where $\bar\sigma_t$ is `ets.se` (0 if $bce_t = 0$), $\sigma_e$ the semi-elasticity of the sector's group (per USD
per t CO2) and $\vartheta$ = 0.5 the effectiveness of output-based allocation (auctioned allowances count fully).

If emissions respond to the price as $\ln(\text{covered}/bce) = \bar\sigma\, V\, p$, the price that meets the cap is
([A1.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A1-1)):

$$
\hat p^{E}_t = \begin{cases}
\dfrac{\ln(cap_t / bce_t)}{\bar\sigma_t\ V} & on_t = 1,\ 0 < cap_t < bce_t,\ \bar\sigma_t < 0,\ V > 0 \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-em-est}

The permit price used is the override row if the switch is on, else the fast estimate:

$$
p^{E}_t = on_t \times \begin{cases}
ovr_t \ (\text{blank: the carbon price path } NCT_t) & \texttt{ETSPriceOverride} = \text{Yes} \\
\hat p^{E}_t & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-em-pe}

$$
\tilde p^{E}_t = p^{E}_t\, V, \qquad \rho = 1 / V
$$ {#eq-em-ptilde}

where $\tilde p^{E}$ is the tax-equivalent price (`ets.pe`) and $\rho$ the revenue factor (`ets.rf`), the permit
price per dollar of tax-equivalent price. All prices are USD per t CO2, real.

### Effect on fuel use and revenue {#sec-em-ets-effect}

The ETS replaces the carbon tax in covered sectors: the new carbon tax applies only where $\kappa_{e,t} = 0$
(@sec-prices). The tax-equivalent price splits by the OBR share ([M1.3](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-3),
[M1.4](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-4)):

$$
A_{e,t} = \tilde p^{E}_t\ \kappa_{e,t}\ (1 - \omega_{e,t}), \qquad
\Sigma_{e,t} = \big(b^{fb}_{G(e),t} + reg_{e,t}\big)\, a\ \mathbb{1}[\text{feebate covers } e] + \tilde p^{E}_t\ \kappa_{e,t}\ \omega_{e,t}
$$ {#eq-em-split}

where

- $A_{e,t}$ is the **price wedge**, the auctioned part (`etr`, USD per t CO2). Times the CO2 factor of each fuel, it
  enters the after-tax fuel price, so usage and efficiency both respond, as for a carbon tax (@sec-prices,
  @sec-demand);
- $\Sigma_{e,t}$ is the **shadow price** (`shpx`): the ETS part, the free (OBR) share, is added to the feebate and
  regulation shadow price. It acts only on the efficiency margin of fuel use, as feebates do, and raises no revenue.

New-policy revenue includes the price wedge times the revenue factor $\rho$: the permit price on the auctioned
part of covered emissions. In power, the new-policy revenue deducts $em_{k,CO_2}\, A_{pow}\, (1 - \rho)$. VAT on new
policies is levied on the tax-equivalent ETS cost. The revenue equations are in @sec-fiscal.

### Meeting the cap {#sec-em-ets-meet}

The fast estimate uses one semi-elasticity, so the full model, where the response comes from prices and elasticities
by fuel and subsector, does not hit the cap exactly. After CO2 is known, the model reports covered emissions, the
gap and a proposed price for the next iteration:

$$
cov_t = \sum_e em_{e,t}\ \kappa_{e,t}, \qquad gap_t = \frac{cov_t}{cap_t} - 1
$$ {#eq-em-gap}

$$
lr_t = \frac{\ln(cap_t / bce_t)}{\ln(cov_t / bce_t)}, \qquad
p^{next}_t = \begin{cases} \hat p^{E}_t & p^{E}_t \le 0 \text{ or } lr_t = 0 \\ p^{E}_t\ lr_t^{\,\beta} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-em-next}

where

- $cov_t$ is covered CO2 (`co2.ets`), $em_{e,t}$ the CO2 of ETS sector $e$ (@eq-em-co2sec);
- $gap_t$ is `co2.gap` (0 if there is no cap), 0 when the cap is met;
- $lr_t$ is the log ratio (`ets.lr`), 0 if $cap_t \le 0$, $cap_t \ge bce_t$ or $cov_t \ge bce_t$ (the cap does not
  bind);
- $\beta$ = 0.5 is the convergence exponent (Settings C15), as legacy's `PricesAdjustedByErrorFactor`;
- $p^{next}_t$ is the proposed price (`ets.next`).

To meet the cap, the proposed prices are fed back into the override row (with the override switch on) and the model
is run again. The goal seek automates this with legacy's damped log-space step:

1. start from the fast estimate, or from the override row if it holds prices (setting `ETSStartFreshContinue`:
   StartFresh always starts from the fast estimate);
2. step $p \leftarrow p\,(p^{next}/p)^{\alpha}$ (a linear step if a price is 0);
3. mix with the previous iterate (weight 0.3) from the second iteration;
4. smooth lightly: 5% weight on a centred 3-year moving average;
5. negative or invalid values keep the current price;
6. halve $\alpha$ when the worst error grows (minimum 0.0625), multiply it by 1.2 when the error more than halves
   (maximum 1);
7. stop when the worst yearly $|cov_t/cap_t - 1|$ over the ETS years is below the maximum error, or after the
   maximum number of iterations.

The goal-seek settings are on sheet `Manual inputs` at their legacy addresses, one value for all scenarios:

| Cell | Name | Setting | Value | Legacy default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E10 | `ETSMaxIterations` | Maximum number of iterations | 20 | 30 |
| E11 | `ETSStartFreshContinue` | StartFresh: start from the fast estimate; Continue: start from the override row if it holds prices | Continue | Continue |
| E12 | `ETSErrorTolerance` | Maximum error: the worst yearly $\lvert cov/cap - 1 \rvert$ | 0.005 | 0.001 |

The values are those the goal seek has always used in Excel-AI; the legacy defaults are for reference (legacy
measures the error on its own criterion). A cell that is not a positive number falls back to 20 iterations and
0.005.

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: the new ETS"}
```
# policies, all years (before the year loop)
for t in years:
    on[t] = NewETS == "Yes" and t >= ETSIntro
    for e in ets_sectors: etsc[e][t] = 1 if on[t] and etscov[e] else 0
    for G in (pow, tra, res, ind):
        etsb[G][t] = 0 if t < ETSIntro else lin(min(t, ETSOutro), ETSIntro, ETSOutro, 1 - ETSAuctStart, 1 - ETSAuctTarget)
    for e in ets_sectors: obr[e][t] = min(1, max(0, etsb[group(e)][t]))
vadj = (1 + ETSCTRisk * imp[ETSVolImpact]) / (1 + vol[ETSVolatility] * imp[ETSVolImpact])
for t in years:
    bce[t] = sum(bco2[e][t] * etsc[e][t] for e)                   # stored scenario-1 CO2
    chg[t] = lin(min(t, ETSOutro), ETSIntro, ETSOutro, ETSChangeRelStart, ETSChangeRelTarget)
    if not on[t]: cap[t] = 0
    elif t > ETSOutro and ETSCapCont == "Constant": cap[t] = cap[t-1]
    else: cap[t] = bce[t] * (1 + chg[t])
    se[t] = sum(bco2[e][t] * etsc[e][t] * semi[e] * (1 - (1 - OBREff) * obr[e][t]) for e) / bce[t] if bce[t] > 0 else 0
    est[t] = log(cap[t] / bce[t]) / (se[t] * vadj) if on[t] and 0 < cap[t] < bce[t] and se[t] < 0 and vadj > 0 else 0
    p[t] = 0 if not on[t] else ((ovr[t] if ovr[t] != blank else cptraj[t]) if ETSPriceOverride == "Yes" else est[t])
    pe[t], rf = p[t] * vadj, 1 / vadj
    for e in ets_sectors:
        etr[e][t]  = pe[t] * etsc[e][t] * (1 - obr[e][t])                       # price wedge
        shpx[e][t] = fb[group(e)][t] * ssc[e] + reg[e][t] + pe[t] * etsc[e][t] * obr[e][t]

# year loop, after CO2
for t in years:
    covered[t] = sum(co2_sec[e][t] * etsc[e][t] for e)
    gap[t] = covered[t] / cap[t] - 1 if cap[t] > 0 else 0
    lr[t] = 0 if cap[t] <= 0 or cap[t] >= bce[t] or covered[t] >= bce[t] else log(cap[t]/bce[t]) / log(covered[t]/bce[t])
    next_p[t] = est[t] if p[t] <= 0 or lr[t] == 0 else p[t] * lr[t] ** ETSNextPriceExponent
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** section 1 rows `ets.on`, `etscov`, `etsc`, `etsb.s`, `etsb.t`, `etsb`, `obr`, `bco2`, `ets.vol`,
  `ets.imp`, `ets.vadj`, `ets.bce`, `ets.chg`, `ets.cap`, `ets.se`, `ets.est`, `ets.ovr` (pasted values), `ets.p`,
  `ets.pe`, `ets.rf`, `ctr`, `etr`, `shpx`; section 13 rows `co2.sec`, `co2.ets`, `co2.cap`, `co2.gap`, `ets.lr`,
  `ets.next`, `bco2.chk`. Inputs on ScenarioDefinition (`NewETS`, `ETSIntro`, `ETSOutro`, `ETSChangeRelStart`,
  `ETSChangeRelTarget`, `ETSCapCont`, `ETSAuctStart`, `ETSAuctTarget`, `ETSPriceOverride`, `ETSVolatility`,
  `ETSVolImpact`, `ETSCTRisk`, coverage rows 99-115); volatility table on Settings rows 16-18; Settings C14
  (`ETSOBREffectiveness`), C15 (`ETSNextPriceExponent`); semi-elasticities on sheet ETSSemi; baseline CO2 on sheet
  BaselineCO2. The goal seek is the macro `SolveETSLive` (the live scenario; `RunAllScenarios` runs it for every
  definition with a new ETS and no override) or the script `ets_goalseek.py WORKBOOK.xlsx <scenario>`, which writes
  the prices to `ets_override_s<scenario>.csv` for pasting into the override row.
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/policies.py`, `prepare()` (ETS block, EQ-M1.3, EQ-M1.4, EQ-A1.1);
  `emissions.py`, `co2()` (covered CO2, gap, `ets.lr`, `ets.next`). The baseline CO2 by ETS sector is read from
  Excel-AI's stored scenario-1 values. CPAT Python has no override row (`ets.ovr` is blank), so with
  `ETSPriceOverride` = Yes the permit price is the carbon price path, and it has no goal seek of its own.
:::

### Limits {#sec-em-ets-limits}

- Power is covered like any other sector: the power model gives its emissions, and the ETS cost enters its
  generation cost (@sec-power).
- Benchmarks are relative to current emission intensity, and output is proxied by fuel use. Free allocation
  therefore moves with emissions, and the OBR share equals the benchmark. Benchmarks by sector are not built yet:
  every group takes the scenario's auctioned proportion.
- The volatility adjustment scales behaviour (the tax-equivalent price), not the permit price.
- No banking, borrowing, price floors or ceilings, and no CBAM process emissions (the legacy CBAM block is placed
  but not read; industrial process CO2 of the inventory is separate and untaxed).

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT"}
- **LD6, L15, L16.** The fast estimate is in log form, $\ln(cap/bce)/(\bar\sigma V)$; legacy's quick estimate is
  linear in the semi-elasticity (L16) and uses a hardcoded relative price of 1.1 (L15), which $V$ replaces. The
  override row is pasted from a Python goal seek with the same damped log-space step, no VBA. Baseline covered
  emissions are data from scenario 1 (`bco2`).
- **LD7, issue I21 (as legacy).** One auctioned share of the scenario for every sector; benchmark = 1 − auctioned
  share, linear from the start to the target year, held after; the sector groups are kept for benchmarks by sector
  later.
- **L78, fixed.** After the target year legacy drops the auctioned share to 0 unless the continuation is Constant.
  The model holds the target share.
- **LD8.** The volatility adjustment $(1 + risk \cdot imp)/(1 + vol \cdot imp)$ from MTInputs rows 95-97 (1/1.1 at
  Medium) applies to the tax-equivalent price and in the fast estimate (legacy row 2191 applies 1/1.1).
- **Methodology.** The methodology describes the ETS as a price set by the user and penalised to a tax-equivalent
  value; the model derives the price from the cap.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Legacy ETS algorithm: inputs and fast estimate"}
Source: `CPAT 1.0pre_456_NoPropData.xlsb`, sheet Mitigation rows 1797-1969 and 2244-2425, sheet Manual inputs
